thread:
jordan: Help — a customer escalated, our function-calling routed to adjust_invoice_line_item instead of refund_payment and it changed invoice lines instead of issuing a refund. Customer has duplicate credit issued.

maya: @jordan can you paste the original request payload + model tool output? :eyes:

jordan: here's the API body we got from the app (redacted):
```json
{
  "input": "Please refund $45.00 for invoice inv_12345 - customer overcharged",
  "tools": [
    { "name": "adjust_invoice_line_item", "schema": {"invoice_id": "string", "amount": "number"} },
    { "name": "refund_payment", "schema": {"payment_id": "string", "amount": "number"} }
  ]
}
```

jordan: model choice log: 
```
Model -> call_tool: adjust_invoice_line_item({"invoice_id":"inv_12345","amount":45})
```

alex: ugh — I can see confusion: both tools accept "amount" and identifiers, the model didn't have a clear signal to prefer refund_payment. Customer lost a refund because line item was adjusted and credit applied. Severity: P2 but billing impact.

maya: do we have schema mismatch tests? this looks like the router picks the first schema-compatible tool. We should patch router priority and add a quick heuristic: if user text contains 'refund' or 'chargeback', bias toward refund_payment.

sam: short-term mitigation: add server-side validation that blocks adjust_invoice_line_item for intents containing 'refund' unless an explicit flag present. I'll open a hotfix.

jordan: repro steps for eng: 1) payload as above 2) model outputs tool name 3) router executes adjust_invoice_line_item with args invoice_id + amount 4) invoice lines changed, credit created instead of a refund.

maya: can you paste the exact model raw output (proto) so we can see why it picked adjust_invoice_line_item?

jordan: raw assistant finish: 
```
{"role":"assistant","content":null,"tool_call":{"name":"adjust_invoice_line_item","arguments":"{\"invoice_id\":\"inv_12345\",\"amount\":45}"}}
```

alex: that confirms tool_call.name was adjust_invoice_line_item. For long term we need: - stricter function schemas (refund_payment requires payment_id) OR - resolver with semantic intent matching + blacklist similar tools.

maya: proposal: update refund_payment schema to require either payment_id OR a field "refund_reason": string. That will make refunds semantically distinct. Also add a unit eval where test prompts containing the word 'refund' must resolve to refund_payment at least 95% of time.

sam: I'll add a telemetry alert for tool-misroute rate spikes and a short runbook for support: how to detect and revert a misapplied line-item adjust.

ops-bot: deploy request queued by sam for branch fix/tool-priority-guard (ci/build 4821) — status: pending.

jordan: customer notified and we issued manual refund while we investigate. Logging note: affected customer id cust_789.

maya: ok next steps: 1) hotfix router bias (sam) 2) schema change + tests (maya) 3) add eval and telemetry (alex) 4) runny postmortem if >5 customers affected.

alex: adding task to billing backlog: BLG-1423.

jordan: thanks team. I'll collect any other similar tickets and add to BLG-1423. :thumbsup:
